chunks: From him, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Ibn Ribat, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the eggs of the sandgrouse (qatā). He said: They are treated like the eggs of the ostrich in the case of camels.

key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: Camels (used here to denote large livestock category)
key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: Sheep/goats (used here to denote small livestock category)
key_terms.بَيْضِ الْقَطَاةِ: Eggs of the sandgrouse, a type of land bird

ai.seo_question: Are the eggs of the sandgrouse permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to eat?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing the permissibility of consuming sandgrouse eggs during Ihram by drawing a legal analogy (*qiyas*) to ostrich eggs, which are treated like camel eggs. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of categorizing birds based on their habitat and mode of consumption, distinguishing land birds from sea creatures, thereby clarifying the scope of prohibited foods for the pilgrim.
